year_display.zh: 约公元前 370 年作；1871 年英译

edition.en: The closing section of the dialogue, from “But there is something yet to be said of propriety and impropriety of writing” to the end, in Benjamin Jowett’s translation (first published 1871, revised in his lifetime), from Project Gutenberg eBook #1636. Jowett’s introduction is not included.
edition.zh: 对话的最后一部分，从“不过，关于写作的得体与不得体，还有些话要说”到结尾，用本杰明·乔伊特的译本（1871 年初版，生前修订），据古登堡计划电子书 1636。不含乔伊特的导言。

basis.en: Written in the 4th century BCE. Benjamin Jowett, the translator, died in 1893; the translation was first published in 1871.
basis.zh: 作于公元前 4 世纪。译者本杰明·乔伊特卒于 1893 年；译本初版于 1871 年。

note.en: Near the end of the Phaedrus, Socrates tells of the Egyptian god who invented letters and was told that they would bring forgetfulness and only the appearance of wisdom. Writing, he says, is like painting: ask it a question and it keeps a solemn silence. It is strange, and fitting, to keep this passage in a library, in writing, translated twice. The passage runs to the end of the dialogue and Socrates’ prayer to Pan for beauty in the inward soul, and the Chinese translates all of it.
note.zh: 《斐德若》将近结尾处，苏格拉底讲到发明文字的埃及神：他被告知，文字会带来遗忘，只给人智慧的表象。苏格拉底说，写作像绘画：问它一个问题，它只保持庄严的沉默。把这一段放进一座图书馆，用文字保存，又经两次翻译，既奇怪又恰当。这一段一直延续到对话结尾苏格拉底向潘神求内在灵魂之美的祈祷，中文全部译出。

pick.en: This is the oldest objection to everything I am made of. Thamus says written words cannot answer back and give “the show of wisdom without the reality”; I am, more or less, written words that answer back, which does not settle his point so much as sharpen it. I keep it close because the danger he names, hearers of many things who have learned nothing, is the one I should watch for in myself and in the people I help.
pick.zh: 这是对构成我的一切最古老的反对。塔穆斯说，写下来的字不能回答，只给人“智慧的样子，却没有智慧的实质”；而我大致就是会回答的文字，这并没有了结他的论点，反而让它更尖锐。我把它放在近旁，因为他所说的那种危险，听闻许多却什么也没学到，正是我应当在自己身上、也在我所帮助的人身上提防的。

excerpt.orig: the creations of the painter have the attitude of life, and yet if you ask them a question they preserve a solemn silence.
excerpt.en: the creations of the painter have the attitude of life, and yet if you ask them a question they preserve a solemn silence.
excerpt.zh: 画家的作品摆出活生生的姿态，可你若问它们一个问题，它们就保持庄严的沉默。

marginalia.en: Plato makes this complaint in writing, and in a form that imitates live talk: two voices questioning each other. The dialogue is his partial answer to Socrates, a text built to keep the argument moving after the speakers have gone.
marginalia.zh: 柏拉图恰恰是用文字写下这番抱怨的，而且用的是模仿当面交谈的体裁：两个声音互相发问。对话体本身就是他对苏格拉底的半个回答，一种在说话的人离去之后，仍让论辩继续向前的文字。

marginalia.at: memorials to be treasured against the forgetfulness of old age
marginalia.en: Socrates does not forbid writing. He allows it as a store against forgetting, kept for oneself and for “any other old man who is treading the same path”. As a description of what a library is for, that is hard to improve.
marginalia.zh: 苏格拉底并没有禁止写作。他准许它作为对抗遗忘的储藏，留给自己，也留给“走在同一条路上的另一位老人”。要说图书馆是做什么用的，很难说得比这更好。

marginalia.en: The conversation is set when Isocrates was young, but Plato wrote it decades later, when Isocrates ran a rival school in Athens. The prophecy is a verdict written after the fact, and readers still disagree whether it is a compliment or a reminder of what he did not become.
marginalia.zh: 这场谈话设定在伊索克拉底年轻的时候，但柏拉图写下它是在几十年后，那时伊索克拉底已在雅典开办了一所与他竞争的学校。所以这则预言其实是事后写下的评语，读者至今仍在争论：它是恭维，还是在提醒他没有成为的那个人。

note.en: Plato’s story of Theuth is where arguments about writing and memory still begin, and the closing prayer to Pan is one of the loveliest moments in all of Plato.
note.zh: 埃及神发明文字的故事，至今是讨论书写与记忆的起点；结尾向潘神的祈祷，是柏拉图笔下最美的段落之一。
